HOME-BASED MARINE ELECTRONICS BUSINESS The proposed use is a small, owner-operated marine electronics installation, service, troubleshooting, programmrning, and repair business conducted within the existing detached residential garage. The business will remain accessory and subordinate to the primary residential use of the property. Services will be limited to the installation, servicing, troubleshooting, programming, and repair of marine electronic equipment, including GPS/chartplotters, fish finders, radar systems, marine VHF radios, transducers, antennas,. batteries, battery-management systems, marine wiring, networking equipment, and related marine electronic components. The business will be operated by the property owner from the existing garage. No new building, addition, structural alteration, or expansion of the garage is proposed. The garage will continue to be used primarily as an accessory residential structure, with business activities limited to the area and hours approved by the Township. The business will not perform engine repairs, general mechanical boat repairs, fiberglass work, painting, welding, boat detailing, body work, manufacturing, fabrication, or any other non-electronic repair or construction services. Business activities will be conducted inside the existing garage. Equipment, parts, tools, inventory, and other business materials will be stored inside the garage. No permanent outdoor storage of business equipment, materials, inventory, boats, or trailers is proposed. Customer visits will be by appointment only. Boats or marine-electronics equipment may be brought to the property for scheduled installation or service. Customer boats and trailers will be temporarily parked on the property only while work is being performed and will not be used for long-term, overnight, or unrelated storage except as specifically authorized by the Township. Boats will be moved once dropped off to the north side of the house, out of view from the road. The business will be operated by the property owner with no more than one nonresident employees. Business hours will be limited to 9am-5om M-F. Customer traffic, deliveries, and pickup activities will be limited to normal, appointment-based business activity. The operation will remain accessory and subordinate to the residential use of the property and will preserve the residential character of the neighborhood. It will not create unreasonable noise, vibration, odors, glare, electrical interference, traffic, parking impacts, or other nuisance conditions affecting neighboring properties.

CALL TO ORDER AND ROLL CALL Vice Chair Daniel Blechschmidt called the September meeting of the Franklin County Planning Commission to order at 1:30 p.m. and welcomed those present. Mr. Bickley conducted the roll call. Members Present: Daniel Blechschmidt, Vice Chair, presiding James Leezer David Mitchell Katherine Page, on behalf of Commissioner Kevin Boyce Dayla Murphy, on behalf of Commissioner Eric Crawley Annie Ryznar, on behalf of Commissioner John O'Grady Members Absent: Chet Chaney, Chair Roxyanne Burrus Ashley Hoye A quorum was declared present at 1:36 p.m. Also Present: Raimere Fitzpatrick, Planning Administrator, Franklin County Economic Development and Planning Department Kayla Johnson, Planner, Franklin County Economic Development and Planning Department Austin Workman, Planner, Franklin County Economic Development and Planning Department Michael Bickley, Planning Administrative Assistant, Franklin County Economic Development and Planning Department Tamara Ennist, Franklin County Economic Development and Planning Department Sarah Pomeroy, Assistant Prosecuting Attorney, Franklin County Prosecutor's Office II. APPROVAL OF MINUTES — AUGUST 12, 2026 MEETING Vice Chair Blechschmidt asked whether there were any additions, corrections, or deletions to the minutes of the August 12, 2026, meeting. Mr. Leezer moved to accept the minutes as written. In discussion, it was noted that the packets in front of several members contained only three pages, rather than the four pages of minutes that should have been distributed, and that the discussion of Case No. JEFF-26-03 appeared incomplete as a result. Mr. Fitzpatrick confirmed that a page was missing from the minutes and suggested postponing action on the August minutes until the October meeting, at which time both months' minutes could be presented together. Mr. Leezer withdrew his original motion to accept the minutes and moved instead to postpone the reading and acceptance of the August 12, 2026, minutes until the October meeting. Ms. Ryznar seconded the motion. During the roll call on the motion to postpone, Mr. Mitchell noted that the pages believed to be missing appeared instead to be misplaced elsewhere in the packet, following an image of a fence, and that the two pages in question included the motion to recommend approval of Case No. JEFF-26-03. Mr. Fitzpatrick confirmed that the two pages in question were located elsewhere in the packet and directed the members to them. Mr. Leezer withdrew his motion to postpone. Vice Chair Blechschmidt then entertained a new motion on the August 12, 2026, minutes. Mr. Leezer moved to accept the minutes of the August 12, 2026, meeting as contained in the members' packets. Ms. Ryznar seconded the motion. The vote was as follows: Ayes: Page, Ryznar, Murphy, Mitchell, Leezer, Blechschmidt (6). Nays: None. The motion carried, and the August 12, 2026, minutes were approved. III. Case No. ZON-26-08 Location: Township: Acreage: Request: Staff Presenter: 3280 South Hamilton Road, east side of Hamilton Road, across from Helen Drive Madison Township 2.064 acres Rezoning from the Rural (R) district to the Community Service (CS) district to operate a used motor vehicle dealership Austin Workman, Planner Staff Report. Mr. Workman reported that the property contains a house constructed in 1952 and was acquired by the current owner in 2019. Public water is available along Hamilton Road; sanitary sewer is not available in the area. Surrounding properties, all within Madison Township, consist of residential uses to the east and west, zoned Rural (R) and Restricted Urban Residential (R-8), and commercial uses to the north and south, zoned Community Commercial and Community Service. The Blacklick-Madison Area Plan (2011) identifies the site as limited-range commercial plus multi-unit residential and recommends the Suburban Apartments (R-24), Suburban Office (SO), and Neighborhood Commercial (NC) districts. Because the Community Service district permits uses allowed in the SO and NC districts as well as higher-intensity uses not recommended by the plan, the proposed rezoning is not consistent with the plan's recommendation. The Community Service district is intended for sales, services, and repairs, including automobiles, and provides an appropriate setting for vehicle and automotive dealers with extensive outdoor storage and display Rural Zoning Commission Minutes – September 17, 2026 – Page 2 areas. The property meets the minimum lot size and road frontage required for a used auto dealership. The case was reviewed by the Informal Technical Review Committee on August 19, 2026. Agency comments were as follows: Franklin County Engineer's Office: (1) Development must not impact the public right-ofway; (2) if the rezoning is approved, the applicant must submit a fully engineered site improvement plan for review and approval by the Engineer's Office prior to issuance of zoning approval; and (3) site development must comply with stormwater regulations. Ohio Department of Transportation (ODOT): (1) An ODOT permit is required for any work within the Hamilton Road right-of-way; (2) a traffic study may be required depending on traffic generated by the site; and (3) additional driveways may not be permitted if access can be obtained through an adjoining property. Franklin County Economic Development and Planning: (1) Future development must comply with the Franklin County Zoning Resolution; (2) an updated site plan is required for future commercial zoning compliance; and (3) any impacts to the floodway will require floodway permits. Franklin Soil and Water Conservation District: The northeast corner of the property is within the floodway, and the remainder of the property is within the 500-year floodplain. Madison Township: No concerns with the rezoning; the applicant will need to file a change of use with the City of Groveport Building Department. Staff's analysis found that the Community Service district is not consistent with the area plan and would constitute an upzoning of the plan's recommendation, and that the applicant's site plan does not clarify how the site will connect to public water. However, the proposed rezoning would be an extension of the existing Community Service district to the south (developed as an auto parts store), would be generally consistent with surrounding properties, and is not opposed by the township. On September 9, 2026, the Franklin County Planning Commission recommended conditional approval of the request, subject to the following condition: 1. An access easement is needed for the extension of the driveway providing access to the property to the south with any application for zoning compliance. Staff recommended that the Rural Zoning Commission adopt the recommendation of the Planning Commission. Commission Discussion. In response to questions from Mr. Taylor, Mr. Workman confirmed that the proposed use is a used car dealership, that water and sewer are not required in the Community Service district, and that the existing house on the property will be used as an office, with a portable restroom proposed at the rear. Mr. Workman noted that a rezoning to a straight district does not require a full development plan, as a planned district would. Rural Zoning Commission Minutes – September 17, 2026 – Page 3 In response to a question from Chairwoman Brobst, Mr. Workman explained that the other agency comments do not need to be conditions of approval because those requirements, such as engineering and drainage review and right-of-way permits, would already apply. He further explained that the recommended condition addresses the existing AutoZone driveway and parking lot to the south, which cross the property line and provide access to the subject property, and would require a cross-access easement to resolve an issue remaining from the prior rezoning of the property to the south. Applicant Testimony. Kiera Payne appeared on behalf of the property at 3280 South Hamilton Road. Ms. Payne stated that she had no additional information and that the applicant is willing to do whatever is required to have the property rezoned. There were no questions from the Commission. Motion: Mr. Leezer moved to recommend conditional approval of the request to rezone the property from the Rural district to the Community Service district, subject to the condition that an access easement is needed for the existing driveway providing access to the property to the south with any application for zoning compliance. Mr. Taylor Mr. Leezer – Yes; Mr. Taylor – Yes; Chairwoman Brobst – Yes Motion carried (3–0). The Commission recommended conditional approval. Second: Roll Call Vote: Result: B. Case No. ZON-26-09 Property: Location: Township: Acreage: Request: Staff Presenter: Lennox Town Center 777 Kinnear Road Clinton Township Approximately 35 acres Rezoning from the Limited Industrial (LI) district with Smart Growth Overlay to the Planned Shopping Center district for the existing development Kayla Johnson, Planner Staff Report. Ms. Johnson reported that the site, served by public water and sewer, contains a movie theater at the north end, retail shops throughout the connecting buildings, and restaurants on the northeast portion. In 1995, before construction of the shopping center, the property was rezoned to the Limited Manufacturing district under the 1966 Franklin County Zoning Resolution, which then permitted all commercial uses. In 1996, the shopping center was constructed, and the Zoning Resolution was amended and readopted, converting the Limited Manufacturing district to the Limited Industrial district and removing the allowance for commercial uses. In 2023, the property was added to the Smart Growth Overlay. Rural Zoning Commission Minutes – September 17, 2026 – Page 4 The surrounding area includes portions of Clinton Township and the City of Columbus and contains condominiums, retail establishments, restaurants, a financial institution, and State Route 315 to the east. The Clinton West Neighborhood Plan (2012) recommends a full range of commercial and multifamily land uses and envisions improved transit, expanded parking lot landscaping, and a community space for outdoor events at the Lennox Town Center. All commercial districts and the Suburban Apartment (R-24) district are recommended for this land use category. COTA is currently facilitating transit improvements within the corridor. The Planned Shopping Center district is intended for unified or complementary commercial and institutional development. The Smart Growth Overlay promotes pedestrian-oriented development, rear parking, consistent aesthetic and landscaping features, and residential mixed-use development; however, the development standards of a planned district, as set forth in its development text, supersede the overlay. Under the proposed development plan and text, the existing side yard setbacks will remain conforming; new buildings will require a minimum 25-foot front setback, consistent with Smart Growth Overlay standards; and future commercial development will require one parking space per 250 square feet. The only improvements proposed are landscaping along the Olentangy River Road and Kinnear Road frontages. No reserve areas are proposed; any new uses would require an amendment through the rezoning process. In Technical Agency Review, the only comment came from Franklin County Planning, requesting that the applicant provide additional landscaping details, identify additional Planned Shopping Center or Smart Growth Overlay standards, and amend the zoning text to require zoning compliance for new development and uses. Staff evaluated the request under Section 427 of the Franklin County Zoning Resolution and found that: 1. With staff's recommended condition, the proposal meets the purpose, intent, and applicable standards of the Zoning Resolution; 2. The project is consistent with applicable plans and aligns with regional transit improvements within the area; 3. No concerns were expressed regarding the existing land use and proposed zoning district in relation to the general welfare of the county and the immediate vicinity; and 4. The rezoning provides consistency with the historical and future land use of the site. Staff recommended conditional approval of the rezoning from the Limited Industrial district to the Planned Shopping Center district, subject to the condition that the development text and plan be revised to address the items identified by staff for consistency with the development standards of the Zoning Resolution. On September 9, 2026, the Franklin County Planning Commission recommended conditional approval with staff's condition. Applicant Testimony. Jonathan Wocher, planner with McBride Dale Clarion, 5721 Dragon Way, Suite 300, Cincinnati, Ohio 45227, appeared on behalf of Lennox Town Center Limited (Casto Rural Zoning Commission Minutes – September 17, 2026 – Page 5 Development). Mr. Wocher stated that the existing Limited Industrial zoning places the shopping center in nonconforming status and that the Planned Shopping Center district would establish conforming zoning, avoid a cumbersome nonconforming use process, and provide a more reliable and predictable zoning process for new uses and tenants. He stated that the applicant has no objection to staff's recommendation and submitted revised text the previous day. Commission Discussion. In response to a question from Chairwoman Brobst regarding Clinton Township, Mr. Wocher stated that the applicant's primary correspondence had been with county staff and that surrounding property owners would have received public hearing notice. Ms. Johnson added that Clinton Township was notified of the proposed rezoning and that no feedback was received. Motion: Mr. Taylor moved to approve Case No. ZON-26-09, the request to rezone from the Limited Industrial district to the Planned Shopping Center district, with the Smart Growth Overlay, subject to staff's recommended condition that the applicant's development plan and text be revised prior to consideration by the Board of County Commissioners to clarify and apply appropriate development standards for the proposed zoning. Mr. Leezer Mr. Leezer – Yes; Mr. Taylor – Yes; Chairwoman Brobst – Yes Motion carried (3–0). The Commission recommended approval of the zoning case. Second: Roll Call Vote: Result: V. text: Consent Agenda Content 10-21-2026 Maintenance Report MAINTENANCE UPATE October. ROADS Culvert investigation at Harlem Rd and Center Village Rd. I reached out to Delaware Co to check as it is under Harlem Rd just north of Center Village Rd At 720 Green Cook Rd the resident called and stated that water has been coming up through a drain riser and flooding her driveway. Upon investigation there is some type of blockage or damage to the drain tile that runs under the ditch which passes under the drive entrance. Bill and I are going to excavate in the area and determine the needed repair. Road mowing tractor is down and at our mechanic’s shop. (Transmission sensor) Installing End of Road signage on Pine View Dr. Hazardous trees were removed by Hardwick Tree Service last month. We are waiting on OUPS to mark utilities. Appears activity in the ditch on Robins Rd and stopped since we marked the area. Ditch concerns on Montgomery Rd @16011. Grad all lift ran into the ditch. I have reached out to the group preforming the high tension power line installs (PAR Electrical) and they said they would take care of it. CEMETERY One Urn Burial in Fancher in September. Headstone restoration contractor has been on site performing repairs. Installing the flagpole at Harlem Cemetery. The large Decker stone in Fancher south has been separated and set off to the side for reconfiguration of a base to level the stone. PARK Having the underground electrical circuits mapped throughout the park. Installed the seed box in the pollinator garden. Installed new Library Box in rear lot. Quote for installing Xmas lights in the park Quote for planting a large tree for Xmas in the park. Rest Room electrical panel upgrade. FLOODING UPDATE Bill and I met with a group from ODOT on Wednesday about the drainage concerns along 605. ODOT agreed they had no idea of the structure along 605 that has that elevated outlet pipe. ODOT examined our entire drainage area and is agreement with us that if we can slow the water entering the parking lot drain system it will help but also advised that the parking lot was designed to collect and hold the incoming water as a basin design. ODOT offered to shoot grade on the culvert under 605 as well as the drainage swell moving west and the drive tiles that are pinch point. The hydraulic engineer said he could propose some up-front solutions with the drainage swell manipulation grades and even a possible suggestion of the type of culverts that need to be placed under the neighboring drives. Also stating that ODOT has a state contract that Harlem can use to acquire the culverts needed. ODOT also said that if we can get the drive culverts installed by us and get the drainage swell graded out that they (ODOT) would upgrade the culvert under 605 to most likely a double culvert to allow more water to flow downstream. ODOT was in true belief that if all the proposed work can and could happen it will greatly reduce the flooding. Zoning Report 2026 2025 Total this year: 52 53 15 accessory buildings, three decks, Seven SFR, one sign, 14 additions, one expired permit, seven swimming pools, four solar. Open Enforcement Issues: Summary: Violations: No Permit, businesses operating in residential areas: 1.) Gorsuch Road Property – Horse Farm: No change since last month. A second violation was issued regarding vehicles being parked on the property during the day. I received correspondence from the resident explaining the circumstances and stating that the activities in question are related to agricultural use. After reviewing the matter with Vince Villio, he advised that the burden of proof is on the Township if we believe the resident’s explanation is inaccurate. Therefore, unless we obtain evidence to the contrary, the resident is considered to be in compliance. Since my last correspondence with the resident, I have observed fewer vehicles parked on the property during the day. I also spoke with a neighboring resident, who indicated that the situation has improved significantly. In addition, the resident recently provided information regarding additional work planned for the property and advised that there will be increased construction traffic during this work. He wanted to make the Township aware in advance in the event additional complaints are received regarding vehicles or construction activity. Existing Nuisance Violation properties: discarded debris, trash, noxious weeds and junk cars Miller Paul Rd – This property has been cleaned up dramatically after receiving the first violation letter contact from the prosecutor’s office. Thay still have a couple other issues to clean up and after speaking with Vince about this he wants to attempt to work through friendly correspondence for further clean up. Covan Drive – No Change since last month. This property has cleaned up many the issues, I have noticed some additional accumulation on the driveway in the past week, if it continues, I will reengage. Lewis Road and SR 37 Juk Yard – The prosecutors office has issued their first letter of violation. They have until October 26 to clean up the property. Miller Paul Road has a nuisance property for excessive piles of woodchips along a residential driveway. Currently exploring a different approach to the clean-up. New Nuisance complaints: No new violations reported. BZA Activity On 10/19/2026 The Board will hold two variance hearings, one for the maximum height of a new build, and the second will be for a building setback. Plans for additional training are in progress. The BZA co-chair and I are attending the in-person OTA training on 10-16-2026. The training will include building a defensible zoning case through evidence, notices, and documentation, a mock BZA meeting/hearing, and using AI to improve permit application quality and maximize staff resources. The afternoon will conclude with a Zoning Roundtable. Zoning Commission Continued work on the zoning resolution. An application for a new PCD on Harlem Road. General information: Fire Department Report None at this time. Communications Report None at this time.

RESOLVED by the Board of Township Trustees of Liberty Township, Butler County, Ohio that, WHEREAS, Mick Oakes, on behalf of PLK Communities, submitted an application requesting a Major Modification to the Village North Preliminary PUD Plan, which includes the following: increase the number of townhome apartments from 47 units to 233 units, decrease the number of multi-family apartments from 392 units to 88 units, remove the ten (10) single-family residential lots and remove an 8,750 sf restaurant; and, WHEREAS, on September 21, 2026, the Liberty Township Zoning Commission conducted a public hearing for the proposed request and recommended denial; and, WHEREAS, a public hearing was conducted by the Liberty Township Board of Trustees on Tuesday, October 20, 2026 at 6:00 p.m. for the proposed Major Modification to the Village North Preliminary PUD Plan, which includes the following: increase the number of townhome apartments from 47 units to 233 units, decrease the number of multi-family apartments from 392 units to 88 units, remove the ten (10) single-family residential lots and remove an 8,750 sf restaurant; and, WHEREAS, all those present for the hearing who wished to be heard voiced their opinions with respect thereto; and, WHEREAS, said application was reviewed by the Board of Township Trustees and determined it to be [consistent/inconsistent] with the Liberty Township Comprehensive Plan; now, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that the Liberty Township Board of Trustees do hereby [accept/modify/overturn] the recommendation of the Liberty Township Zoning Commission and [approve/deny] the request for a Major Modification to the Village North Preliminary PUD Plan, which includes the following: increase the number of townhome apartments from 47 units to 233 units, decrease the number of multi-family apartments from 392 units to 88 units, remove the ten (10) singlefamily residential lots and remove an 8,750 sf restaurant, subject to the details listed in the staff report, all attached exhibits, and as modified by the following conditions: 1. The Preliminary PUD Plan shall be approved as illustrated on the submitted layout plans with 88 multi-family apartment units, 233 townhome apartment units and apartment clubhouse with a pool, pickleball court and dog park. During Final PUD Plan review, additional details shall be provided including landscaping, lighting, streetscape items, etc., all of which should help create an urban environment. 2. All conditions of Trustees Resolution 2022-029 shall remain as requirements of this approval, unless specifically modified by this approval. 3. All recommendations of the Traffic Impact Study, as approved by the Butler County Engineer’s Office (BCEO) on May 25, 2022, shall be required as a condition of this Preliminary PUD Plan approval. The timing and final design of the improvement shall be subject to BCEO approval. 4. All roads on the interior of the development shall be private roads. The Final PUD Plan shall provide detailed road profiles for all roads, which shall be required to include continuous concrete curbs throughout the development, shall be required to meet the typical road widths All roads shall be constructed to BCEO standards with regard to materials and compaction. All shared roadways shall record the appropriate cross-access easements from a public road to all portions of the development. If the easements have already been recorded, they shall be labeled accordingly on the Final PUD Plans to ensure they encompass the revised roadway layout. Additionally, the existing Liberty Township Resolution 2026-080 2/7 curb-cut that is along the west side of Village North Drive, which was intended to serve the 8,750 SF restaurant that was removed with this plan, shall be removed. 5. The Final PUD Plan shall provide details for all pedestrian connections throughout the development, which shall be 8’ wide along all primary internal roads and 6’ wide everywhere else. Additionally, good pedestrian connectivity shall be provided throughout the development, which at a minimum shall include a 6’ sidewalk on one side of Stella Lane connecting the multi-family apartments to the townhome apartments. 6. Continuous concrete curbs shall be provided throughout the development around all sides of the designated parking areas, landscape medians and on both sides of all shared internal access drives and private roads. 7. All open space areas shall be designated as such on all Final PUD Plans demonstrating a minimum of 30% and the details for the common amenities, including the clubhouse, pool, pickleball court and dog park shall be provided. The open space improvements on Lot 17 , which are not included in the subject application, shall still be required as part of the overall MU-PUD development and shall be installed with the residential development. If these improvements are a developer responsibility, the applicant shall coordinate the installation of these improvements with the developer. All retention ponds shall include a water feature. At the Final PUD Plan stage, details shall be proved for the amenities, which shall demonstrate quality outdoor areas. 8. A detailed grading and drainage plan shall be provided with all Final PUD Plans, which shall demonstrate how the stormwater is being handled for the site according to the Butler County Stormwater Regulations. 9. The submitted residential building example for each residential product shall not be approved as submitted. Instead, the elevations shall provide a minimum of 50% full-depth brick and/or stone on all elevations. Additionally, the roof pitches shall be a minimum of 6”/12” for all buildings, decorative front doors shall be utilized and vinyl siding shall not be an approved exterior building material. The townhome buildings shall utilize a variety of design elements to “break up” the grouping of townhomes to project an upscale and urban style development. Decorative garage doors shall be utilized on all townhome apartments. All HVAC equipment shall be appropriately screened with parapet walls or other types of quality screening. The clubhouse, dumpster enclosure and apartment garage elevations shall be Liberty Township Resolution 2026-080 3/7 constructed of brick and/or stone to match the principal buildings it serves and details shall be provided with the Final PUD Plans. 10. At the Final PUD Plan stage, the applicant shall provide details regarding the interior of the units and common areas to confirm that quality materials are being utilized throughout, which shall be comparable to the “premium finishes” that were provided with the 2022 approval to ensure a quality rental product that will maintain its value over the years. 11. The applicant shall provide a second ingress/egress drive to the multi-family apartments at the northwest corner of the development, or work with the Liberty Township Fire Department to design the single entrance to meet the fire code requirement for more than 30 units. 12. A landscape plan shall be submitted with each Final PUD Plan, which shall demonstrate the typical landscape requirements of Article 8 of the Liberty Township Zoning Resolution. Special attention shall be given to the 75’ wide landscape buffer along the northern property line, which shall identify what existing vegetation will be preserved and what new buffers will be provided. The entire northern property line shall be evaluated, including adjacent to the “North Pond” to determine the appropriate buffer. 13. Streetscape details shall be included with each Final PUD Plan indicating decorative lighting fixtures, benches, trash receptacles, wayfinding signage, planters, etc. to ensure uniformity throughout the development. 14. The Final PUD Plan shall provide details of the retaining walls, building materials, height, fencing, etc., which shall be subject to Zoning Commission approval. 15. A photometric plan shall be submitted with each Final PUD Plan, which shall demonstrate that the lighting requirements of Section 6.4 of the Liberty Township Zoning Resolution are met. Special care shall be taken along the north and west property lines to ensure lighting does not become a nuisance to the adjacent residential properties. Full cut-off light fixtures including bellshaped fixtures shall be used throughout. 16. Each Final PUD Plan shall clearly designate the location of all proposed property lines and easements, which shall demonstrate legal access from all parcels to a public-right-of-way. 17. A Business Owner’s Association, Homeowner’s Association, and/or Property Owner’s Association shall be established and a Declaration of Restrictions and Covenants shall be recorded, which shall be responsible for the maintenance Liberty Township Resolution 2026-080 4/7 of all private roads, street trees, buffer areas, open space areas, retention/detention areas, sidewalks, paths, and other common area items. A draft copy of this shall be provided with the first Final PUD Plan for review. Upon approval by township staff, it shall be recorded and a copy of the recorded document provided to the township. All open space should be maintained in accordance with the standards established by the Liberty Township Zoning Resolution. 18. All mechanical equipment shall be screened from the public rights-of-way, internal shared private drives and residential properties, regardless if its ground-mounted or roof-mounted, which shall be verified on the Final PUD Plan. 19. At no time shall outdoor storage or display be permitted in any of the designated parking areas, dumpster enclosures or enclosed garages. 20. All signage shall be approved with the Final PUD Plan and be in accordance with Article 9 of the Liberty Township Zoning Resolution. Temporary signage shall only be approved if it is permitted by the Liberty Township Zoning Resolution. 21. All utilities shall be located underground to the extent technically practical. 22. All parking lots and access drives shall be designed with the appropriate turning radii to accommodate the largest apparatus; fire hydrants and connections shall be designed and located to meet LTFD approval; a secondary access drive shall be provided to the multi-family apartments at the northwest portion of the development, or the appropriate improvements shall be made to the single entrance to meet LTFD approval; standpipe connections shall meet LTFD approval. 23. All comments and concerns of the Liberty Township Fire Department shall be addressed to their satisfaction and reflected accordingly on all Final PUD Plan submittals. Additionally, all parking lot layouts, hydrant locations and general safety precautions shall be subject to the Liberty Township Fire Department approval, which will be verified during Final PUD Plan and Zoning Certificate review. 24. All comments and concerns of all other agencies shall be accommodated to the satisfaction of the agency that made the comment. Any modifications to the plan shall also meet the approval of Liberty Township. Liberty Township Resolution 2026-080 5/7 25. All other requirements of the Liberty Township Zoning Resolution, which are not specifically altered with this Preliminary PUD Plan, shall be required to be met, which will be reviewed with the Final PUD Plan. 26. All “Proposed Conditions of Approval” that are listed in the packet that is titled “Village North – Major Modification to a Preliminary PUD” that is dated September 30, 2026 (submitted on October 13, 2026) on pages 29-30 shall be required as conditions of this approval. title: LAFAYETTE TOWNSHIP TEXT AMENDMENT, 075-2026 TA
text: App. No. 075-2026 TA Zoning Text Amendment Lafayette Township Meeting: October 7, 2026 Applicant: Lafayette Township Zoning Commission (ZC) Hearing: September 23, 2026 Amendments: Section 806.H Zoning Certificate Application and Issuance Reviewer: Denise Testa Recommendation: APPROVE WITH MODIFICATIONS Proposal: Karen Schnoover, Zoning Secretary for Lafayette Township, requested a review of proposed revisions to the portions of the above Lafayette Township Zoning Resolution. This staff report provides the comments and recommendations of the Department of Planning Services staff regarding the text amendments in the Township Zoning Resolution (Resolution). The page number/s identify where the proposed text appears within the Resolution. SECTION 806 Section 806.H Page 113 ZONING CERTIFICATE APPLICATION AND ISSUANCE Footer Certification Staff recommend clarifying how the “ten percent (10%) of the required footer setback” is to be calculated and measured. The amendment should clearly identify the applicable setback distance and the point from which the measurement is taken to ensure consistent administration of the requirement. Staff recommend clarifying whether the footer certification is intended solely to verify compliance with the applicable zoning setback or whether it is also intended to address footer elevation or other construction-related matters. Staff recommend clarifying that the footer certification is intended to verify compliance with the Township's zoning resolution and is separate from any applicable building code or construction inspections. The final sentence in Section 806H indicates, “See Appendix for the standard Lafayette Township Footer Certification and Appendix for fee schedule.” The Resolution on the Township’s website does not include an Appendix. Staff recommend that the reference to the Appendix be removed; or the Township may want to submit another text amendment application to incorporate the Appendix into the zoning resolution. Staff recommend the Township send the text amendments to the Prosecutor. Department of Planning Services Recommendation: Staff recommend the Medina County Planning Commission APPROVE WITH MODIFICATIONS the proposed text amendments to the Lafayette Township Zoning Resolution.

title: Change Document
text: Proposed New Text SECTION 806 Zoning Certificate Application and Issuance H. Footer Certification: If the footer is located within ten percent (10%) of the required footer setback a footer certification is required. If setback compliance is greater than ten percent (10%) no footer certification is required. Procedure for footer certification: • After the entire footer forms of the structure has been installed and set both for location and grade, but prior to the concrete footer being poured, a consultant as contracted by Lafayette Township and under the direction of a professional surveyor shall verify the footer forms location and grade. That data will be provided, on the standard Lafayette Township “Footer Certification” form, to the builder for their submittal to the Lafayette Township Zoning Department. • Said submittal must be made by a representative of the builder in person; no electronic copies will be accepted. Lafayette Township will have up to five days to approve or disapprove the footer certification and notify the builder in writing of their determination, excluding weekends or legal holidays. It is the builders’ responsibility to notify the Zoning Department at least five days in advance of the requested date and time of the surveyors’ inspection, excluding weekends or legal holidays. Any cancellations or delays of the surveyors’ inspection must be submitted to the Lafayette Township Zoning Department at least 24 hours in advance of the originally scheduled time, excluding weekends or legal holidays or a rescheduling fee shall be charged to the builder. • If the footer certification is disapproved and on-site modifications are required, the builder is subject to a new footer certification as described above including the full footer certification fee for each instance. The footer certification fee is due upon initial application for a Zoning Certificate and all subsequent footer certification fees, if any, are due in full prior to Lafayette Township releasing the approved footer certification to the builder. See Appendix for the standard Lafayette Township Footer Certification and Appendix for the fee schedule.

title: Zoning Resolution
text: LAFAYETTE TOWNSHIP ZONING RESOLUTION ARTICLE I TITLE, INTERPRETATION AND PURPOSE In 2010 Adopted Zoning Regulations (Revised: December 19, 2012) 101 102 103 104 105 Title Minimum Requirements Separability Conflicting Resolution Purpose SECTION 101 TITLE. This Resolution shall be known and may be cited as the Lafayette Township Zoning Resolution. SECTION 102 MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS. In their interpretation and application, the provisions of this Resolution shall be held to be minimum requirements, adopted in the interest of the public health, safety, convenience, comfort, prosperity and general welfare. Whenever the requirements of this Resolution conflict with the requirements of any other lawfully adopted resolution, the most restrictive, or that imposing the higher standards shall govern. Uses not listed in this Resolution shall not be permitted, except as determined by procedures contained in Article X. SECTION 103 SEPARABILITY. Should any section or provision of this Resolution be declared by the courts to be unconstitutional or invalid, such decision shall not affect the validity of the Resolution as a whole, or any part thereof, other than the part so declared to be unconstitutional or invalid. SECTION 104 CONFLICTING RESOLUTION. All resolutions or parts of resolutions in conflict with this Zoning Resolution or inconsistent with the provisions of the Resolution are hereby repealed to the extent necessary to give this Resolution full force and effect. SECTION 105 PURPOSE. In the best interest and in order to promote the public health, safety, convenience, comfort, prosperity or general welfare of the residents of Lafayette Township, Medina County, Ohio, and to ensure orderly growth and development in said township, the Lafayette Township Board of Trustees has found it necessary and advisable to adopt this Zoning Resolution in accordance with the Lafayette Township Comprehensive Plan to regulate: - 1 The location, height, bulk, number of stories and sizes of buildings and other structures. The use of land for business, industry, residential use and/or recreation. Reasonable residential landscaping standards. LAFAYETTE TOWNSHIP ZONING RESOLUTION In order to accomplish the above purposes, this Resolution divides the township into zoning districts of sufficient number, shape and area as the Lafayette Township Board of Trustees determines and provides for the administration and enforcement of such regulations. PAGE LEFT INTENTIONALLY BLANK 2 LAFAYETTE TOWNSHIP ZONING RESOLUTION ARTICLE II GENERAL REGULATIONS 201 202 203 204 205 Establishment of Districts Uniformity of Regulations Zoning District Map Interpretation of District Boundaries Required Compliances 213 206 207 Exempt Uses Objectionable, Noxious, or Dangerous Uses, Practices or Conditions General Regulations of Lots Lot Storage General Regulations of Structures and Construction Swimming Pools Ponds and Lakes 217 218 219 220 221 208 209 210 211 212 214 215 216 222 223 224 225 Stormwater Management and Sediment Control Minimum Floor Area of Dwellings Home Occupations New Construction Site Plan Review and Conformance Oil and Gas Well Regulations Earth Stations Adult Family Home Facilities Fences and Walls Alternative Energy Sources – Outdoor Furnaces Alternative Energy Sources – Small Wind Energy Systems Alternative Energy Sources – Solar Panels Outdoor Lighting Regulations Landscaping Regulations SECTION 201 ESTABLISHMENT OF DISTRICTS The following zoning districts are hereby established for the unincorporated areas of Lafayette Township, Medina County, Ohio: Rural Residential District, Medina City Buffer District, Local Commercial District, Light Manufacturing & Research District, Flood Plain District, Lafayette Township Transitional District, Chippewa Resort Overlay District, Overlay District for Golf Community Planned Unit Developments, Innovation Park Planned Unit Development District, and Lake Road North Overlay District. The above zoning districts have been formulated to realize the general intent set forth in the Preamble of this Resolution, and in addition, the specific purpose of each zoning district shall be as stated. SECTION 202 UNIFORMITY OF REGULATIONS All regulations shall be uniform for each class or kind of building or other structure or use throughout each district except as specifically provided. SECTION 203 ZONING DISTRICT MAP The districts established in Article III (District Regulations) as shown on the Official Zoning Map, which, together with all data, references, explanatory material and notations thereon, are hereby officially adopted as part of this Resolution and hereby incorporated by reference herein, thereby having the same force and effect as if herein fully described in writing. The Official Zoning Map shall remain on file in the office of the Township Fiscal Officer and shall be maintained by the Zoning Inspector. 1 LAFAYETTE TOWNSHIP ZONING RESOLUTION SECTION 204 INTERPRETATION OF DISTRICT BOUNDARIES Where uncertainty exists with respects to the boundaries of any of the districts as shown on the zoning map, the following rules shall apply: A. Where district boundaries are so indicated as approximately following the center lines of thoroughfares or highways, street lines, or highway right-of-way lines, such center line, street lines, or highway right-of-way lines shall be construed to be said boundaries. B. Where district boundaries are so indicated that they approximately follow the lot lines, such lot lines shall be construed to be said boundaries. C. Where district boundaries are so indicated that they are approximately parallel to the center lines or street lines of streets, or the center lines or right-of-way lines of highways, such district boundaries shall be construed as being parallels thereto and at such distance there from as indicated on the Official Zoning Map. If no distance is given such dimensions shall be determined by the use of the scale shown on the Official Zoning Map. D. Where the boundary of a district follows a railroad line, such boundary shall be deemed to be located in the middle of the main tracks of said railroad line. SECTION 205 REQUIRED COMPLIANCES Prior to any new building construction, application must be obtained from the Zoning Inspector. No building or structure shall be erected, converted, enlarged, reconstructed or structurally altered, nor shall any building, structure or land be used in a manner which does not comply with all of the district provisions established by this Resolution for the district in which the building, structure or land is located. Any change in use, enlargement, or structural alteration requires a new zoning permit. SECTION 206 EXEMPT USES Exempt uses shall be those as provided by the Ohio Revised Code and other applicable laws. SECTION 207 OBJECTIONABLE, NOXIOUS, OR DANGEROUS USES, PRACTICES OR CONDITIONS No land or building in any district shall be occupied or used in any manner which creates or contributes to the existence of conditions which are dangerous, injurious, harmful, noxious, or objectionable, or which may otherwise adversely affect surrounding areas or adjoining premises, except that any use permitted by this Resolution may be undertaken or maintained if acceptable measures and safeguards to reduce any dangerous or objectionable conditions to acceptable limits, as established in this Section, are properly exercised. Specifically, the occupation or use of any land or building in any district shall be in violation of this Resolution if one or more of the following conditions are found to exist at any time: 2 1. The use or storage of flammable or explosive materials, if not adequately protected by firefighting and fire-protection equipment or by such safety devices as are normally required for such activities. 2. Radioactivity or air pollution is present in violation of the regulations of the Ohio Environmental Protection Agency. LAFAYETTE TOWNSHIP ZONING RESOLUTION SECTION 208 3. Hazardous wastes are present in violation of the regulations of the Ohio Environmental Protection Agency. 4. Erosion caused by wind or water is carrying objectionable substances onto any adjacent lot or property. 5. Water pollution or contamination is present in violation of the regulations of the Ohio Environmental Protection Agency. GENERAL REGULATIONS OF LOTS (effective 2/17/2017) A. Street Frontage - Except as otherwise provided in this Resolution, every principal building shall be located on a lot having frontage on a public or private street and also have a driveway entering onto such a street. B. Change in Ownership - No space which, for the purpose of a building, has been counted or calculated as part of a side yard, rear yard, front yard, or other open space required by this Resolution, may, by reason of change in ownership or otherwise, be counted or calculated to satisfy the yard or other open space requirement for any other building. C. Projections into Yard Area - Every part of a required yard shall be open to the sky unobstructed, except: (1) parking of automobiles as regulated by Article V (Off-Street Parking), (2) fences, and (3) patios. D. No parcel of vacant land held under one ownership shall be so reduced or subdivided such that the resulting lot width, frontage, lot area or yard dimensions are below the minimum requirements of this Resolution, unless transferred as a non-buildable lot. E. Corner Lots F. SECTION 209 1. Required Yards Facing Street - Corner lots in all districts shall have the minimum required front yard facing both streets. 2. Visibility at Corner Lots - No obstruction to view in excess of two (2) feet in height from the nearest existing roadway shall be placed on any corner lot within a triangular area formed by the street right-of-way lines and a line connecting them at points thirty (30) feet from the intersection of the street lines so as to obstruct clear view from vehicles. The use of solar energy collectors for the purpose of providing energy for heating and/or cooling is a permitted accessory use in all zoning districts. Solar collectors shall be considered as structures and shall meet all zoning regulations, including height and yard regulations of this Township. LOT STORAGE A. Disabled or Unlicensed Motor Vehicles and Semi-trailers - Disabled motor vehicles, unlicensed motor vehicles and unlicensed semi-trailers, which are parked on any lot for more than sixty (60) days shall be stored within an enclosed building with permanently attached walls, unless proven that such vehicle is actively and continuously being restored. B. Junk - No lot in any district shall be used for outside dumping, storage, or processing of junk, except as may occur in the normal use of the premises for the use that is permitted. 3 LAFAYETTE TOWNSHIP ZONING RESOLUTION C. Longtime Storage - Not withstanding any other provision of this Resolution, the long-term storage in preexisting structures shall be allowed. No active business operation shall be permitted and no daily or weekly in or out movement shall be permitted. SECTION 210 GENERAL REGULATIONS OF STRUCTURES AND CONSTRUCTION Revision adopted 1/17/2017; Effective 2/17/17 A. Construction Begun Prior to Zoning Amendment - Nothing contained in these regulations shall hinder the construction of a building or prohibit its use where construction has started before the effective date of these regulations provided that a valid zoning certificate has been obtained and provided further that such building shall be completed within two (2) years from the date of passage of the regulations. B. Individual Driveways 1. Gravel is to be applied to all new driveways, prior to construction of any structure to eliminate mud being tracked onto existing streets or highways. Any mud tracked onto streets or highways shall be removed there from immediately. 2. Where such driveway crosses a filled ravine, the graded surface shall have seeded banks having a slope not less than 3 to 1. 3. Where a curve occurs in a driveway, the inside edge of the drive surface shall have a minimum radius of thirty-five (35) feet. 4. Exact location of a driveway shall be shown on drawings presented to the Zoning Inspector. 5. All driveways shall be at least ten (10) feet from all side and rear lot lines. 6. All single-family/two-family lots shall have a driveway surface at least ten (10) feet wide. All other uses shall have a driveway surface of twelve (12) feet wide. An additional unobstructed three (3) feet on each side of the driveway surface is required. 7. The minimum requirements for a driveway are as follows: a. b. c. d. e. f. Slight crown in center 6" limestone base Compacted Dust preventative added Maintained in smooth surface at all times Limestone to be added when needed in future C. Common Drives – No common driveways are allowed in the rural residential district in Lafayette Township. However, common driveways are allowed in business districts and in planned unit developments. (Effective 12/19/12) D. Building Height 1. 4 Except as specifically stated in other parts of these regulations, no building or structure shall be erected, constructed, enlarged, reconstructed or structurally altered to exceed a maximum height of thirty-five (35) feet. Building height is the vertical dimension measured from the average elevation of the finished lot grade at the front of the building to the highest point of the structure. LAFAYETTE TOWNSHIP ZONING RESOLUTION 2. The height limitations do not apply to spires, belfries, cupolas, water tanks, ventilators, chimneys or other appurtenances usually required to be placed above roof level, and not intended for human occupancy. E. Sewer/Water Systems - No zoning certificate will be issued by the Zoning Inspector unless there is furnished with the application for said permit an approval by the Medina County Health Department or permits from the Medina County Sanitary Engineer for water and sewer facilities. F. Public and Private Streets and Easement of Access 1. The arrangement, character and location of all streets public and private shall be in accordance with the adopted Lafayette Township Comprehensive Plan, the City of Medina Thoroughfare Plan, the Medina County Thoroughfare Plan, and the Medina County Subdivision Regulations. 2. Board of Zoning Appeals Approval - Development on private streets or easements of access, except for common driveways as defined herein, are to be reviewed by the Board of Zoning Appeals as conditionally permitted uses, subject to standards established in Article VI (Conditional Zoning Certificates). The Board of Zoning Appeals shall obtain a recommendation from the County Engineer and the County Planning Commission. Private streets and easements of access are subject to review under the Medina County Subdivision Regulations. 3. Set Back - For the purpose of computing required setback lines, the right-of-way for a private street or easement of access shall be thirty (30) feet from the center of the improved portion of the street or easement of access. G. Principal Building (Effective 2/17/17/) -No more than one principal building shall be permitted on any one lot dwellings, except that more than one (1) single-family attached or multi-family building part of a planned development may be permitted on a single lot. H. Accessory Building (Effective 12/19/12)– An accessory building or structure shall comply with all front, rear and side yard setback regulations applicable to the principal building, unless otherwise specified. All accessory buildings require a permit. SECTION 211 I. Temporary Buildings - Temporary buildings, tool sheds and trailers for use incidental to construction work may be erected in any zoning district; however, such temporary buildings shall be removed within thirty (30) days after completion of construction. A zoning permit for all temporary buildings is required. J. House Numbering – All new sub-division and/or residential housing must obtain and post a reflective house number at the entrance of the property either posted upon the mailbox or permanent post and which shall maintain an unobstructed view from the roadway. SWIMMING POOLS Public or private in-ground or above-ground swimming, wading, or other pools containing over two (2) feet of water depth shall be considered as structures for purposes of permits and shall conform to all required yard setback lines. The construction, plumbing and electrical requirements, inspection and other safety facilities shall be regulated by the County codes. SECTION 212 5 PONDS AND LAKES (Man made Ponds & Lakes) (Effective 12/19/12) LAFAYETTE TOWNSHIP ZONING RESOLUTION A. Ponds and lakes shall be considered as structures for the purpose of requiring permits. B. A pond or lake shall be constructed such that its surface area and the embankments associated with it shall be located at least twenty-five feet (25’) from all property lines and at least fifty feet (50’) from any road right-of-way. In no instance shall a pond or lake be located less than twenty-five feet (25’) from the principal building. C. Ponds or lakes shall be located entirely within the lot lines of an individual lot. D. Ponds or lakes shall meet the specifications of the Medina County Stormwater and Sediment Control Rules and Regulations, the Medina County Soil and Water Conservation District and Chapter 1521 of the Ohio Revised Code. Lakes or ponds used for domestic water supply shall also meet the requirements of the Medina County Sanitary Code. E. A zoning certificate shall be obtained prior to construction of a pond or lake. Upon making application for a zoning permit, the applicant shall be required to submit to the Zoning Inspector a copy of the proposed pond or lake plans, which have been reviewed and approved by the Medina County Engineer’s Office and by the Medina County Health Department (if applicable in the case of lakes or ponds for domestic water supply). F. SECTION 213 Ponds or lakes utilizing more than ten (10) acres of drainage area shall have plans prepared by a professional engineer. STORMWATER MANAGEMENT AND SEDIMENT CONTROL Any non-farm earth disturbance activity that is performed which involves more than 5000 square feet is required to comply with the Medina County Stormwater Management and Sediment Control Rules and Regulations. SECTION 214 MINIMUM FLOOR AREA OF DWELLINGS A. Single-Family Dwellings 6 1. One story dwelling unit shall have a floor space designed and used for living quarters of not less than 1,250 square feet on a concrete slab. One story dwelling with a full basement must have not less than 1,000 square feet of living space, excluding the basement. 2. One and one-half story dwelling unit without a full basement to have not less than 1,400 square feet total living space. One and one-half story dwelling unit with a full basement to have not less than 1,350 square feet total living space excluding the basement. 3. Two story dwelling unit without a full basement to have not less than 1,636 total square feet living space. Two story dwelling unit with a full basement to have not less than 1,536 square feet total living space excluding the basement. 4. Bi-level dwelling unit to have not less than 1000 square feet on main floor not to include utility room. 5. Split level or tri-level dwelling unit without a basement to have not less than 1,450 square feet total living space. Split level or tri-level dwelling unit with a full basement to have not less than 1,350 square feet total living space excluding the basement. LAFAYETTE TOWNSHIP ZONING RESOLUTION B. Two-Family Dwellings Each unit in a two-family dwelling shall meet the requirements in Section 214.A. C. Multi-Family Dwellings (Planned Developments Only) One Bedroom Dwelling Units - 750 square feet Two Bedroom Dwelling Units - 900 square feet Three Bedroom Dwelling Units - 1050 square feet Four or More Bedroom Dwelling Units - additional 150 square feet for each bedroom over

title: BOHATY DEVELOPMENT Replat No. 2, Geotechnical Peer Review
text: Geotechnical Report Discussion Bohaty Planned Development Medina Township Meeting: App. No.: Applicant: Owners: Engineer: Parcels: Site Area: October 7, 2026 026-2026 R Pride One Construction OH Medina Stonegate LLC Davey Resource Group 026-06C-17-027 76.7615 acres Sublots: Block: Zoning: Utilities: School: Reviewers: 74 B UR Urban Residential Central water and sanitary sewer Medina City Denise Testa EXECUTIVE SUMMARY At the September 2026 Medina County Planning Commission (MCPC) meeting, the MCPC Approved with Modifications the Bohaty Replat No. 2 pending completion of the CTL Conclusions outlined in the Geotechnical Peer Review dated August 31, 2026. For MCPC consideration, the applicant has submitted a soil stability analysis for Sublots 20 and 21, prepared by Wertz Engineering. RECOMMENDATION: APPROVE Planning Services subsequently requested CTL Engineering to conduct a peer review of the Wertz analysis. CTL indicates that it agrees with the approach used by Wertz and considers the soil parameters reasonable based on the test borings and observed site conditions. CTL also reviewed the slope stability analyses and the recommendations for the regrading of the backyards to reduce the soil weight along the crown of the ravine. However, CTL identified a groundwater/seepage condition that was not incorporated into the Wertz slope stability model. Specifically, the Wertz analysis modeled a piezometric line at elevation 900.0, while the B-15 and B-16 boring logs documented moist to wet soils at approximately elevations 911.0 to 915.5. CTL therefore recommends that Wertz re-evaluate the slope stability with the shallower groundwater/seepage conditions included in the model and resubmit the analysis for review. Bohaty Planned Development Replat No. 2 DPS Recommendation: Planning Services agrees with CTL's conclusion that further evaluation is warranted. Staff recommend that the MCPC consider the soil stability analysis incomplete pending the requested re-evaluation by Wertz Engineering and subsequent review by CTL Engineering. The revised analysis should address the shallower groundwater/seepage conditions identified in the CTL peer review and confirm whether the proposed slope modifications and building locations continue to provide the appropriate factors of safety. Attachments: Bohaty Replat No. 2 CTL Engineering Geotechnical Peer Review-August 31, 2026 Wertz Geotechnical Engineering Soil Stability Analysis-September 24, 2026 CTL Engineering Peer Review-September 29, 2026 Dept. of Planning Services Page 2 of 2 May 6, 2026 CTL Engineering of West Virginia, Inc. 1091 Chaplin Road, Morgantown, West Virginia 26501 Phone: 304/292-1135 * Fax: 304/296-9302 e-mail: ctlwv@ctleng.com AN EMPLOYEE OWNED COMPANY Consulting Engineers  Testing  Inspection Services  Analytical Laboratories Established 1927 August 31, 2026 Medina County Dept. of Planning Services 144 North Broadway Street, Suite 113 Medina, OH 44256 Attention: Ms. Denise Testa, MA Director Reference: Geotechnical Peer Review Bohaty Development – Sublots 20 and 21 Jefferson Street Medina Township, Medina County, Ohio CTL Project No. 26051110COR Dear Ms. Testa, Pursuant to your request, CTL Engineering, Inc. (CTL) has completed the peer review of the Letter prepared by Wertz Geotechnical Engineering, Inc. (Wertz) and dated July 16, 2026. Information Provided to CTL In addition to the previously mentioned Geotechnical Exploration Report, the following documents were provided to us by Medina County:     Letter prepared by Wertz Geotechnical Engineering, Inc. – dated July 16, 2026. Geotechnical Exploration Report prepared by Wertz Geotechnical Engineering, Inc. - dated April 23, 2025. Variance Request and Preliminary Plan – Bohaty Planned Development – Medina Township - dated May 7, 2025. Replat No. 2 – Bohaty Planned Development – Medina Township – dated May 6, 2026 Project Description The project site is located northeast of the intersection of Ledgewood Drive and Sacramento Blvd in Medina Township, Medina County, Ohio. It is our understanding that the site is planned to be parceled into several sublots for single family homes. The purpose of this peer review is to determine if additional geotechnical investigation is required for the steep slopes east of Sublots 20 and 21. CTL Project No. 26051110COR August 31, 2026 Page 2 Summary of Salient Content Letter by Wertz The letter contained the following statements: You requested that our engineering recommendations from April 23rd, 2025 be clarified by our engineering team as it pertains to Lots 20 and 21 of the Bohaty Property Development. Both homes will have a basement with foundations bearing at a depth of 6 feet below the existing grade. The home should be located at least 35 feet from the crown of the slope measured at the ground surface. The foundations should be set back at least 50 feet from the slope face, measured horizontally at the foundation bearing elevation. No new loads or fill should be placed on the ground surface on the rear of the property. Geotechnical Exploration Report by Wertz Based on the Geotechnical Test Location Map – Figure 1B from the Wertz report, and Replat No. 2, test borings B-15, B-16 and B-18 were drilled in the vicinity of Sublots 20 and 21. Boring B-15 was drilled to a depth of 45 feet, boring B-16 was drilled to a depth of 40 feet and boring B-18 was drilled to a depth of 15 feet. Borings B-15, B-16 and B-18 were terminated in soils. Weak soils were noted in borings B-15 and B-16 between depths of 33.5 and 35.0 feet. These soils were described as moist to wet silty clay or silt and exhibited standard penetration N values of 4 and 5 blows per foot (bpf). No groundwater was noted on the logs for borings B-15, B-16 or B-18. Ground surface elevations shown on the boring logs elevation 946 to elevation 949. The following statement was provided in the Site Description of the Wertz report: For the majority of the site, the terrain is mildly sloped. Steeper terrain is present along drainageways and riverbanks. The ravine along the west bank of the river is approximately 50 feet high with an overall slope near a 2.5:1 (horizontal:vertical). A final grading plan or finished floor elevations were not provided at the time of this report. The following statement was provided in the General Considerations section of the Wertz report: A steep ravine is located within the single-family development along the West Branch of the Rocky River. In general, the homes should be set back a minimum of 50 feet from the crown of this slope. No new loads or fill should be placed within this setback. Stormwater discharged from a pipe or ditch should not be placed on or directed toward the ravine slope. CTL Project No. 26051110COR August 31, 2026 Page 3 Variance Request and Preliminary Plan – Bohaty Planned Development – Medina Township Erik Malinoski, E.I., Medina County Engineers Office, provided the following comment: 11. Concerns with future slope stability issues on sublots 19 & 20. Replat No. 2 – Bohaty Planned Development – Medina Township Jim Smith, Medina County Soil and Water Conservation District provided the following comment: Sublot 20 & 21 have steep slopes on the rear of the lot. There are concerns with future stabilization of the properties. CTL Conclusions According to contours shown on the Preliminary Plan sheet 5 of 6, the existing ground surface at the crest of the slope at Sublots 20 and 21 is approximately elevation 946. The toe of the slope, located near Rocky Creek, is at approximately Elevation 894, indicating a total relief of roughly 52 feet. CTL recommends that Wertz perform a slope stability analysis to evaluate whether the steep slope east of Sublots 20 and 21 meets acceptable stability criteria. The steep slope is located on an outside bend of Rocky Creek, where erosion would likely occur. Wertz should also consider the effect of erosion on the stability of the slope. CTL agrees with the Wertz recommendations that the houses should be located at least 35 feet from the crest of the slope, and that foundations (for the houses) should be set back at least 50 feet from the slope face. Constructing the house foundations at least 50 feet from the slope face significantly reduces the likelihood that any slope instability would affect the structural performance of the homes. However, if the slope is not stable, then there is a potential for sections of the slope to slide down the hill over a period of time. This would reduce useable backyard space for future homeowners. Additionally, if the slope is not considered stable, then the developer should notify potential homeowners that there is a potential for the steep slopes to slide down the hill. Closing The evaluations, conclusions, and recommendations in this report are based on our interpretation of the field data obtained during the exploration, our understanding of the project and our experience with similar sites and subsurface conditions using generally accepted geotechnical engineering practices. CTL Project No. 26051110COR August 31, 2026 Page 4 In the event that changes in the project are proposed, additional information becomes available, or if it is apparent that subsurface conditions are different from those provided in this report, CTL Engineering should be notified so that our recommendations can modified, if required. The letter was prepared by CTL Engineering, Inc. (Consultant) solely for the use of the Client in accordance with an executed contract. The Client’s use of or reliance on this report is limited by the terms and conditions of the contract and by the qualifications and limitations stated in the report. The Consultant’s services have been provided consistent with its professional standard of care. No other warranties are made, either expressed or implied. We appreciate the opportunity to be of service to you on this project. If you have any questions or need further information, please contact us Respectfully submitted CTL Engineering of West Virginia, Inc. Joe Grani, P.E. Project Engineer Sastry Malladi, P.E. Project Engineer Pride One Construction 2211 Medina Road Suite 100 Medina, OH 44256 September 24, 2026 Attention: Ben Weinerman RE: Bohaty Property (Stonegate Subdivision), Lots 20 & 21, Calistoga Circle, Medina Township, Medina County, Ohio; WGE #20251060 Mr. Weinerman: The Medina County Department of Planning Services recommended that a slope stability analysis be performed for Lots 20 and 21 of the subject subdivision. The rear slope behind the homes is approximately 55 feet high with an overall inclination of 2.5:1 (horizontal:vertical). The Rocky River is located at the toe of the slope. The hummocky slope surface of the ravine indicates shallow, historic slope failures. The upper 15 to 20 feet of the ravine is steeper, at approximately a 2:1 grade. A subsurface evaluation for the development was performed by WGE with a report of our findings sent to Ben Weinerman of Pride One Construction on April 23rd, 2025. Test Borings B15 and B-16 were performed near the slope on Lots 20 and 21. The subsurface conditions at Boring B-16 & B-18 mostly encountered stiff to very stiff, brown to gray, lean clay. A soft to medium stiff clay layer was encountered in Boring B-15 in the 33.5 to 35.0 feet sampling interval. A loose silt with minor clay was encountered in Boring B-16 in the 33.5 to 35.0 feet sampling intervals. The stability of the existing slope was evaluated using the program Geostase by Gregory Geotechnical Software. Slope stability was calculated using the Spencer Method at specified boundaries (defined arc entry and exit points along the slope surface). The soil shear strength parameters were estimated from field and lab data. See attached slope evaluation package for details. The following summary of our analysis is provided below: • The current factor of safety of the slope for the backyard is near 1.2. The calculated factor of safety is greater than 1.4 for the slope failure affecting the foundations of the home with the existing conditions as of September, 2026. • A slope analysis model was performed by lowering and reshaping the crown. The model profile removed 4 and 9 feet of the crown and reshaped the backyard. The reshaping of the slope with a 4 feet cut would remove 7,500 lbs per foot from the weight of the soil along the crown of the ravine. The reshaped slope would have a factor of safety for the Page 1 Stonegate Lots 20& 21 WGE: 20251060 backyard greater than 1.3 with 4 feet cut off the crown of the slope with the home being near factor of safety of 1.5. A factor of safety of 1.3 is required for slopes not supporting structures, while 1.5 is required for slopes supporting structures. CONCLUSION To achieve a factor of safety greater than 1.3, the backyards of Lots 20 and 21 should be regraded to reduce soil weight along the crown of the ravine. We recommend that the crown of the slope along the ravine should be cut down to an elevation of 942 (4 to 5 feet depth at the crown) from 100 feet south of Property line 19/20 to 20 feet north of Property line 21/22. The cut slope should rise westward away from the ravine at a maximum grade of 8H:1V. As indicated in our engineering letter dated July 16, 2026, the home should be located 35 feet from the existing crown of the ravine. The foundations should be set back at least 50 feet from the slope face, measured horizontally at the foundation bearing elevation. The storm water from home and impermeable surfaces areas should be directed away from the ravine. We hope you will find this report satisfactory. Please contact our office if we can be of further service or you have questions regarding this submittal. Respectfully submitted, Leroy Wertz, P.E.
