title: HERITAGE RUN ESTATES, 081-2026 CP, Wadsworth Township – 9:00 a.m
text: Concept Plan Heritage Run Estates Wadsworth Township Meeting: App. No.: Applicant: Engineer: Parcels: Site Area: October 21, 2026 081-2026 CP Highmark Development Davey Resource Group 038-17C-27-004/32-006/ 33-012/33-013 94.2 acres Sublots: Zoning: Utilities: School: Reviewer: 31 Sublots I-2 Heavy Industrial R-R Rural Residential Private Septic and Private Wells Wadsworth City Denise Testa EXECUTIVE SUMMARY The 94+ acre site is located south of Wall Road, north of Eastern Road and west of Pifer Road. The applicant proposes 31 sublots and three streets leading to permanent three permanent cul-de-sacs. ADJACENT ZONING/LAND USE Direction North Zoning I-2 Heavy Industrial (Township) R-R Rural Residential (Township) I-2 Heavy Industrial East R-R Rural Residential (Township) South R-R Rural Residential (Township) West R-R Rural Residential (Township) I-2 Heavy Industrial (Township) Proposal: The applicant proposes the following: • 31 sublots ranging between 2+ and 9+ acres for single-family homes; • Three streets leading to three permanent cul-de-sacs; and • Four stormwater management basins with one also functioning as a fire pond. Access: Access to the site is proposed at Wall Road connecting to a new street, Hickory Grove Drive, and leading to three permanent cul-de-sacs; Wall Road for Sublots 27, 28, 29 with a common access drive; and Pifer Road for Sublots 30 and 31. Land Use Single-family homes Agricultural fields Wall Road Single-family homes Forest Residential homes Eastern Road Cropland Pifer Road, Single-family homes Railway Company Heritage Run Estates Concept Plan Site Conditions: The property consists primarily of land used for agriculture. Riparian corridors are located on the western portion of subdivision. The Ohio Department of Natural Resources Oil and Gas Well locator indicates a plugged and abandoned well, 21658, is located on Parcel 038-17C-27-004 on Sublot 1. 2007 Wadsworth Township (Township) Comprehensive Plan The Comprehensive Plan did not address the I-2 Heavy Industrial zoning district. According to the 2007 Township Comprehensive Plan, the Light Industrial land use category, “…applies to those areas that are primarily industrial in use but are in proximity to residential land uses. The proximity of these areas to residential uses requires that less intense industrial uses are developed or redeveloped, in order to keep intense industrial uses separate from residential uses. These areas are appropriate for research and development, light industrial and manufacturing, and other industrial uses that will not adversely affect adjacent residential uses. This category comprises approximately 1,426 acres or 9 percent of the Township.” The Future Land Use Map indicates the community prefers these parcels to be zoned as R-R Rural Residential. Wadsworth Township (Township) Zoning Resolution Three of the subject properties are zoned I-2 Heavy Industrial as outlined in Section 405. According to the Township Zoning Regulations, the I-2 zoning district is established to, “…provide for and accommodate light and heavy industrial uses in the fields of repair, storage, manufacturing, processing, wholesaling distribution and disposal, free from the encroachment of residential, retail, and institutional uses. In addition to the residential, commercial and light industrial districts, the uses listed are intended to complete the full range of activities necessary for functioning of a community but because of certain objectionable characteristics should be placed in a separate district.” Dept. of Planning Services Page 2 of 9 October 21, 2026 Heritage Run Estates Concept Plan Tract 4 on the plat is zoned R-1 Rural Residential. Based on the Township Zoning Resolution, the purpose of the R-1 District is to, “…provide for rural residential development at varying densities based on services available at locations throughout the township. This district is intended to allow residential development of sufficiently low density to preclude the creation of public health and safety problems which could result in the need to extend central facilities in an uneconomical fashion. This district is also intended to promote the continuation of the predominant rural character in areas of township where services are not available. This district is further intended to encourage sustainable agricultural uses as a part of the life of the community.” Agency Comments: Italicized text indicates agency comments. Shawn Bouscher Wadsworth Township Zoning Inspector wadsworth.twp.zoningins@gmail.com 330.848.2121 After reviewing the proposed concept development plan the only concern zoning sees is that a variance will be needed for lots 27, 28 and 29 on Wall Road to have a shared driveway and /or easement. It makes perfect sense for this need based on the hills and sight lines on this part of Wall Road. The zoning commission will need to make that call when site plans are reviewed for the development. Mike Stanec Wadsworth Township Fire Department mike.stanec@sharonfire.org 330.239.4992 Fire Pond shall be installed per Medina County specifications to also include the following: 1. A pull-off lane, matching the pavement composition of the adjacent road, shall be provided with the following dimensions: five (5) feet wide, fifty (50) feet long and shall utilize twenty (20) feet long tapers. The pull-off lane shall be centered on the dry hydrant connection point. 2. A minimum of three (3) feet of clear, unobstructed space shall be provided around the dry hydrant. 3. A two (2) inch wide band of white reflective tape should be installed around the entire outside diameter of the exposed PVC pipe. The white reflective tape should be installed approximately three (3) inches below the 90-degree PVC elbow. 4. A Dry Hydrant identification sign shall be installed three (3) feet behind the dry hydrant and shall be oriented to face the pull-off lane. The sign should be four (4) feet above the adjacent grade. 5. The dry hydrant shall be tested by the Fire Department once the pond is filled to verify the flow rate. 6. The common access drive should have a turnaround for emergency vehicles since it is over 150’. WFD would prefer not to have a common access drive for units 27, 28, 29. Recommend having individual drives to Wall Road. Dept. of Planning Services Page 3 of 9 October 21, 2026 Heritage Run Estates Concept Plan Caleb Edwards TC Energy caleb_edwards@tcenergy.com No impact on TC Energy Pipelines. Angela Fritz TC Energy us_crossings@tcenergy.com 800.562.8931 Per engineering review, TC Energy is not impacted by the “Heritage Run Estates Concept Plan” project. Ben Romine Sanitary Engineer’s Office bromine@medinacounty.org 330.723.9575 The sanitary sewer is within the City of Wadsworth FPA and the MCSE does not have water utilities available to service these parcels. Our office does not have any comments. Glenn Davis Wadsworth City gdavis@wadsworthcity.org 330.335.2740 The Wadsworth FPA shows that this property is “Currently Sewered.” The applicant is advised to contact NOACA and/or EPA to determine the appropriate process for a prescription modification in order to authorize septic uses. To be clear, the applicant has requested through a County application to use septic systems without either annexing to the City or connecting to the City's sewer system. They originally considered annexing and connecting to City sewer, but the nearest available City sewer is some distance away and rather expensive. We did not discuss septic options with the applicant. Erik Malinoski: CONDITIONAL APPROVAL County Engineer’s Office emalinoski@medinacounty.gov 330.764.8879 1. 2. 3. 4. 5. Clarify if subdivision will be public or private. If public, a drainage maintenance fund will be required. Provide an additional 10’ of R/W along subdivision frontage. Frontage improvements will be required along Wall Road. Show location of mailbox kiosk. Dept. of Planning Services Page 4 of 9 October 21, 2026 Heritage Run Estates Concept Plan 6. 7. Maintain existing watersheds. Overland flood routes and rear yard drainage conveyance to be included in subdivision drainage design. 8. Show and identify existing road culverts and ditch enclosures. 9. Driveway culvert sizing along Pifer Road to be included with subdivision design. 10. Riparian setbacks are noted as being from the Medina Township Riparian Guide Map. This site is in Wadsworth Township, clarify where riparian setbacks came from. 11. We have concerns with the long-term viability of having a plugged well located underneath a fire pond. 12. Lots 1, 8 & 26 to access the interior subdivision street only. 13. If discharging septic systems are proposed for this subdivision, show where the anticipated discharge location will be. 14. Label the recorded document number for the sanitary easement located on sublot 31. 15. Follow the Engineering Code regulations for Common Drives for the drive serving sublots 27, 28 & 29. Nathan McConoughey Medina County Health Department nmcconoughey@medinahealth.org 330-723-9523 The lots proposed for the Heritage Run Concept Plan will require soil testing conducted by soil scientist(s) and site evaluations for each lot, conducted by this office to determine feasible system options for sewage treatment systems. The lots will also require private water systems as there is no public water supply available. Sewage treatment system options may be limited due to isolation distances required from water bodies/ stormwater ponds, wetlands, existing oil wells, topography etc. Private Water System placement must also meet isolation distances from oil wells, sewage treatment systems, water bodies etc. Additionally, plumbing permits will be required with this office. Jim Smith Medina County Soil and Water Conservation District jsmith@medinacounty.gov 330.722.9317 1. Majority of the soil types on this project site are Canfield Silt loam with 2-6% slopes, Wooster silt loam with 6-12% slopes and 12-25% slopes. Limitations of these soils are slow permeability and slope. In areas where the slope exceeds 6-12%, it is highly recommended to utilized additional stormwater and sediment erosion control practices to minimize erosion effects and downstream impacts. 2. On the plans, there are riparian corridors outlined within the ravines on the western portion of this project site. Setback requirements are to be met throughout all phases of construction. 3. All watersheds and drainage directions must be maintained through all phases of construction. Dept. of Planning Services Page 5 of 9 October 21, 2026 Heritage Run Estates Concept Plan 4. Stormwater basins should have adequate outlets for the watershed to handle the discharge appropriately. 5. There should be a plan in place for who is responsible for maintenance and monitoring of the stormwater basins. Maintenance could include but is not limited to: dam/spillway maintenance, sediment removal, debris removal, and invasive species control. 6. Drainage and overland flow routes should be considered and thought through for sublots 27 & 28. The homes appear to be positioned directly at the confluence of the drainage patterns. 7. Portions of this project site had been agriculture land. Locate and address subsurface drain tile accordingly. 8. It is recommended that tree removal be limited to the immediate construction site. Jen Wisard: CONDITIONAL APPROVAL Medina County Tax Map Department taxmaps@medinacounty.org 330.722.9777 1. 2. 3. 4. 5. 6. 7. 8. Please contact the tax map office to reserve different road names. There is already a White Oak Circle and a Hickory Grove Avenue. Heritage Run Estates has been added to the reserved subdivision name list. It is recommended that the final subdivision plat be submitted to Tax Maps for review, before obtaining signatures. Remove existing parcel numbers from final plat. Any subdivision with Phase numbers or replat number are subject to change at the time of recording. Please contact the email below of the Northern Ohio District USPS, to discuss the location of the centralized collection boxes, so allocation of space for equipment can be made on the subdivision plat. Contact info: kd82p0@usps.gov Subject to Medina County Engineer Land Conveyance Standards found at: http://www.highwayengineer.co.medina.oh.us/surveying/landconveystds.pdf and to all Tax Map Dept. comments from previous Planning Dept. reviews. We defer any comments regarding roadways to the Township Zoning and the Medina County Engineer. Sarah Stanzi Northeast Ohio Areawide Coordinating Agency (NOACA) sstanzi@mpo.noaca.org 216.241.2414 x231 I have prepared the attached consistency review map to confirm the current Facility Planning Area (FPA) boundaries (Wadsworth FPA) and Prescriptions for Wastewater Treatment (“Currently Sewered”) for the parcels associated with the Heritage Run Estates concept plan. In Clean Water 2020, NOACA’s Section 208 Water Quality Management Plan, on-site wastewater treatment systems are an allowable option and are consistent with the plan for areas designated as “Currently Sewered.” Please see the attached excerpt from Clean Water 2020, which outlines the acceptable wastewater treatment options under this prescription. Dept. of Planning Services Page 6 of 9 October 21, 2026 Heritage Run Estates Concept Plan The Highlands of Sharon Phase 3 situation differs from the current proposal. In that case, the area was designated as “Areas Served by On-Site Systems,” and a sanitary sewer extension was being proposed to serve the development. That extension would have conflicted with the existing FPA prescription, and Ohio EPA would not have approved the associated Permit-ToInstall (PTI) without an FPA prescription modification. It is also important to clarify that NOACA does not have the regulatory authority to require individual properties to connect to sanitary sewers. That authority rests with the appropriate health department. Based on the current FPA boundaries and prescriptions, an FPA modification would not be necessary for Heritage Run Estates to utilize on-site wastewater treatment systems, should that be the treatment option ultimately agreed upon. Please let us know if you have any questions or if we can provide any additional information or assistance. Department of Planning Services Staff Comments: 1. The County Engineer’s Office has expressed concern about the long-term viability of locating a fire pond over a plugged and abandoned well. Staff note that the County Engineer is contacting ODNR. 2. Staff recommend the applicant pursue a map amendment and submit the Board of Zoning Appeals’ decision prior to submission of the Preliminary Plan. The Heavy Industrial Zoning District does not allow single family homes as a permitted or conditional use. Staff shared the zoning amendment process with the applicant and Township. 3. Staff recommend the applicant define the building envelopes for each sublot prior to submission of the Preliminary Plan. The stormwater management basins will impact the building envelopes on each applicable sublot. 4. NOACA has clarified that an FPA prescription modification is not required for the proposed on-site wastewater treatment systems under the current designation. The feasibility of individual systems remains subject to applicable requirements and site evaluations by the Medina County Health Department. The applicant should coordinate with the Health Department to establish the anticipated process for demonstrating that each proposed sublot can accommodate a compliant wastewater treatment system and private water supply. The potential effects of the proposed stormwater basins, wetlands, riparian areas, existing plugged well, and other required isolation distances should be considered in evaluating the proposed lot layout. 5. Based on the proposed Concept Plan, Staff recommend the applicant address the following issues related to access and street design prior to submission of the Preliminary Plan. Dept. of Planning Services Page 7 of 9 October 21, 2026 Heritage Run Estates Concept Plan a. Sublots 27, 28, and 29: The Township Zoning Inspector indicates the applicant is required to submit a variance request to construction a shared driveway. Staff recommend the applicant complete the variance request process with the Township prior to submission of the Preliminary Plan. The Fire Department prefers individual driveways; however, this appears to be a preference rather than a requirement. The Fire Department also requests a turnaround for emergency vehicles if a common drive exceeds 150 feet. Staff recommend the applicant contact the Fire Department to clarify these comments prior to submission of the Preliminary Plan. The County Engineer directs the applicant to comply with the County's common access drive requirements. b. Wall Road: The County Engineer identifies additional right-of-way and frontage improvements. c. Pifer Road: Driveway culvert sizing must be addressed. d. Public versus private streets: The County Engineer requests clarification. 6. According to the Medina County Subdivision Regulations Article VI Section 604(D)1 Alternative Roads – Common Access Drives shall meet the following requirements. Staff recommend the applicant comply with these regulations. Common access drives, as distinguished from a private street or road, may be permitted for up to three residential lots. Lot dimensions shall comply with the township zoning in effect. Such drives shall be private, placed within a platted access easement, owned and maintained by the abutting properties, and whose design shall be reviewed and approved by the local County Engineer to ensure safe and adequate access. The following criteria are intended to minimize the amount of roadway conflicts caused by excessive and unmanaged driveways and shall guide the decision of the Planning Commission in approving common access drives. a. Common access drives may only be permitted where adequate site distance is available, according to the standards of the County Highway Engineer’s Office. b. text: Variance Request and Preliminary Plan White Oak Estates Granger Township Meeting: App. No.: Applicant: Engineer: Parcels: October 7, 2026 077-2026 V-PP Pulte Group, Inc. Cunningham & Assoc., Inc. 005-07B-16-028/032/033 005-07B-22-056 Site Area: Sublots: Zoning: Utilities: School: Reviewer: 100.46 acres 39 Sublots R-1 Residential District On-Site Septic and Private Wells Highland Local Denise Testa EXECUTIVE SUMMARY The 100+ acre site is located south of Interstate 271 (I-271), north of Remsen Road and west of State Road. The applicant proposes 39 sublots and one open space block on public streets leading to permanent public cul-de-sacs. The applicant has requested a variance to Section 604(B)(9) Street Stubs and Cul-de-sacs of the Medina County Subdivision Regulations (Regulations) which states that a permanent culde-sac street shall not exceed 2,500 feet in length. The Planning Commission will need to vote on each item separately. VARIANCE RECOMMENDATION: APPROVE PRELIMINARY PLAN RECOMMENDATION: APPROVE WITH MODIFICATIONS ADJACENT ZONING/LAND USE Direction North East South West Zoning R-1 Rural Residential R-1 Rural Residential R-1 Rural Residential R-1 Rural Residential Proposal: The applicant proposes the following to be completed in two phases: • 39 sublots ranging between 2 and 5+ acres for single-family homes; • 2+ acres of open space; • Two public streets leading to two permanent cul-de-sacs; • Two stormwater management basins with one also functioning as a fire pond; • 25-foot riparian setback for all undisturbed wetlands; and • Wetland impacts of 0.4840 acres. Land Use Residential/Deciduous Forest/I-271 Residential/State Road Residential/Deciduous Forest/Remsen Road Cropland/Residential White Oak Estates Variance and Preliminary Plan Access: Access to the site is proposed at State Road creating two public streets that lead to two permanent public cul-de-sacs. Site Conditions: The site has rolling topography, with elevations generally decreasing toward the drainage features located through the southern portion of the property. A mapped stream extends generally from west to east through the southern portion of the area shown on the aerial map. Areas of wooded vegetation and lower-lying ground are associated with this drainage corridor. The site includes abandoned gas wells on proposed Sublots 9, 13, 16, 23/24, 28, 31 and the Open Space Block. Sublot 25 includes a culvert. Several wetland and surface-water features are mapped within and adjacent to the subject property. These include wetland areas and ponds concentrated along the existing drainage corridor, as well as additional ponds and wetland features on adjacent properties. The aerial mapping also depicts wooded areas associated with portions of the drainage system. The subject property is located within the Rocky River drainage basin. The local drainage system includes Allard Creek, which flows to the East Branch Rocky River. In summary, the subject parcels consist of a combination of open agricultural land, wooded areas, rolling terrain, and areas associated with existing streams, drainage features, wetlands, and surface water. The location and extent of these existing physical features are depicted on the aerial and environmental maps included with this report. Granger Township Zoning Resolution The site is zoned R-1 Rural Residential District. According to the Granger Township Zoning Resolution (ZR), the purpose of the R-1 Residential District “…is to manage low-density residential development that will preserve the rural residential character of Granger Township.” The minimum lot size is two acres and the minimum required frontage is 175 feet. The ZR does not require riparian setbacks and does not include a conservation development option for the R-1 District. Staff recommend the applicant consult with the Township Zoning Inspector to ensure compliance with the ZR and confirm the applicable review/approval procedures. Dept. of Planning Services Page 2 of 7 October 7, 2026 White Oak Estates Variance and Preliminary Plan VARIANCE REQUEST 1. Variance Request The applicant has requested a variance from Section 604(B)(9), Street Stubs and Cul-de-sacs, of the Medina County Subdivision Regulations (Regulations), which limits the length of a permanent cul-de-sac street to 2,500 feet. The proposed length of Wojtowicz Way is 3,643 feet, representing an increase of approximately 46 percent over the maximum permitted length, while the proposed length of Cannata Way is 2,890 feet, representing an increase of approximately 15 percent. 2. Site Conditions and Access Considerations. The Granger Township Zoning Inspector has indicated that the Township prefers that access to the subdivision be provided solely from State Road. Although the property has frontage on Remsen Road, establishing an additional access point would require disturbance of the existing creek and could impact the rural character of the area. Staff note that the requested variance allows the subdivision to be designed in a manner that minimizes environmental impacts while accommodating the Township’s preferred access arrangement. 3. Variance Criteria Section 203(A)(2) of the Regulations establishes the criteria for granting variances. Staff comments regarding compliance with these criteria are provided below: a. The MCPC must find that an unnecessary hardship may result from the strict application of the Regulations due to exceptional topographic or other conditions. The combination of the site’s physical characteristics, the presence of the creek, and the Township’s preference for a single access point from State Road creates circumstances that limit roadway design options. Requiring strict compliance with the 2,500-foot standard would likely necessitate additional roadway connections or a significant redesign of the subdivision layout, resulting in greater environmental disturbance. The requested variances represent an approach that balances site constraints with the overall objectives of the Regulations. b. The MCPC may vary the Regulations to relieve an established hardship, provided such relief can be granted without detriment to the public interest and without impairing the intent and purpose of the Regulations or the desirable development of the neighborhood and community. The Regulations state that the cul-de-sac length limitation is intended to promote “greater convenience to traffic, more effective police and fire protection, and efficiency of road maintenance.” The Granger Fire Department has no concerns about the proposed street lengths on the permanent cul-de-sacs. Based on the information submitted, the proposed street lengths do not appear to adversely affect internal traffic circulation or roadway maintenance. Granting the variance would not appear to impair the intent and purpose of the Regulations or the desirable development of the subdivision and surrounding area. Dept. of Planning Services Page 3 of 7 October 7, 2026 White Oak Estates Variance and Preliminary Plan c. The Regulations provide criteria for determining hardship and granting relief but do not establish specific standards regarding the amount of a variance that may be approved. Over the past 19 years, the MCPC has granted five variances related to cul-de-sac length, with approved increases ranging from approximately 5.6 percent to 37.6 percent above the permitted maximum. The average increase granted was approximately 17.7 percent. The requested variance for Cannata Way is generally consistent with prior approvals, while the requested variance for Wojtowicz Way exceeds the range of past approvals and has been evaluated in the context of the site constraints, environmental considerations, Township access preferences, and any comments received from emergency service providers. Recommendation: For further consideration, the applicant has included additional materials in the attached Variance Summary & Exhibits including maps highlighting cul-de-sac street lengths of other Granger Township subdivisions. The Department of Planning Services recommends the Planning Commission to Approve both variances for the White Oak Estates Preliminary Plan. Majority of this project site is made up of Ellsworth silt loam with greater than 2-6% slopes and 6-12% slopes. Restrictions with these soil types are slope, seasonal wetness, slow permeability, a clayey subsoil. Areas of ElC2 soils are classified as moderately erodible. 2. Sublots 10-14, 32 and 33 have wetlands within their boundaries that are planned to be filled. US Army Corps of Engineers and/or Ohio EPA should be involved with plans for impacting wetlands. 3. Stormwater management basins should have a plan that outlines the party responsible for maintenance and monitoring of the dam/spillway of the basin(s). 4. Fire ponds should be approved by the respective township zoning inspector and local fire department. 5. Wetlands on site that are not planned to be impacted should have the riparian setbacks observed and followed throughout all phases of construction. 6. In areas where there’s land disturbance on slopes greater than 6%, it is encouraged to utilize excessive sediment and erosion control practices until the ground has vegetative establishment. 7. Watershed and natural drainage paths should be maintained throughout all phases of construction. 8. It is recommended that tree removal stay limited to the immediate construction area only. It is encouraged to leave healthy trees standing near wetland areas to preserve the soil structure and natural features of the wetlands. This increases stormwater holding capacity, improves water quality, and reduces future risk of erosion. 9. This property had been in agriculture use and may have subsurface drain tile throughout the property. It is recommended to locate and address existing tile accordingly.
